summary: Attempt 2 discharges review findings m1 and m2 (O-001, O-002) with the leaf-based rewrite that was accepted for them. Invoke-HarnessRaw in tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 now reads only mkdtemp's ASCII leaf from the harness's line, with '(?m)^harness: scratch kept at .*[\\/](fsa-rules-[A-Za-z0-9_]+)\s*$'. For each of GetTempPath() and $env:TEMP it then removes [IO.Path]::Combine(folder, leaf) if that folder exists. The printed path is never compared, so an 8.3 short TEMP, a non-ASCII TEMP that say() prints as \xe9, a space in TEMP and TEMP≠TMP are all cleaned the same way. Only a folder with mkdtemp's name directly in TMP or TEMP is ever removed. I added ShortName and NonAscii shapes to tests/bugs/SL-076-ScratchKeptPath.Tests.ps1 and watched them fail on the attempt-1 code. The stand-in now prints through say()'s escaping, and the Python shape runs the real harness.py for all three spellings of TEMP. After the fix they pass, and so do the real RuleCases C-006 and C-014 runs with a short or a non-ASCII TEMP, and the full .NET suite. Neither C-006 run left an fsa-rules-* folder, nor did C-014.

files.why: HF-026 plus review m1 and m2: Invoke-HarnessRaw captures only the fsa-rules-[A-Za-z0-9_]+ leaf from the 'scratch kept at' line. It removes <GetTempPath() or $env:TEMP>\<leaf> when that folder exists. The printed path is not compared, so the space, 8.3, non-ASCII (say() escapes) and TEMP≠TMP spellings are all cleaned.

The HF-026 test. New since attempt 1: a ShortName shape (TMP=TEMP set to Scripting.FileSystemObject's ShortPath of a spaced folder) and a NonAscii shape (TMP=TEMP under 'José Smith', built from [char]0xE9). The stand-in is now a pwsh script that prints through harness.py's say() escaping. Refused gains a case for a folder name mkdtemp never makes. obligations.how: The fix follows m2's leaf-based rewrite, which the decision says also settles m1. No printed parent is compared any more: the leaf is joined to GetTempPath() and $env:TEMP exactly as the process spells them, so an 8.3 TEMP finds its folder. I added a ShortName shape (TMP=TEMP set to FSO .ShortPath, e.g. ...\FS8CED~1\Users\JOHNSM~1\AppData\Local\Temp). On the attempt-1 code it failed ('removes ...\JOHNSM~1\...\fsa-rules-sl076' FAIL). The Python shape's 8.3 spelling also left fsa-rules-qcwe62v9 behind on that code. Both pass after the fix, and RuleCases C-006 with TEMP=TMP=an 8.3 short name held every check and left no fsa-rules-*.

not_built: The send-back suggested deleting 'the exact scratch path it recorded when it made the copy', if the design allowed it. It does not fit here. RuleCases never makes the harness's scratch: harness.py's own tempfile.mkdtemp does, and the only record RuleCases gets is the printed line, which is the source of the four spellings. Recording the exact path would take a new harness option or pointing the harness child's TEMP at a RuleCases-owned folder. The second would also move every dotnet/MSBuild/NuGet scratch file the harness makes. Both go past the design and the accepted m1/m2 decisions, which chose the leaf-based rewrite. The rewrite does keep the send-back's safety requirement: it removes only a folder whose name is exactly mkdtemp's 'fsa-rules-' + [A-Za-z0-9_]+, directly in one of the two folders mkdtemp could have used, and nothing else. Refused pins that with 4 cases.
follow_ups: RuleCases C-006 cannot pass on a machine whose GetTempPath holds a non-ASCII character. Its 'engine root <path>' and '<path>\taad3\fitness.py, not from this root' expectations use the raw path of folders New-TempDir made, while harness.py's say() prints them escaped ('\xe9'). Measured: 4 checks fail with TEMP=TMP under 'José Smith'. The expectations could be escaped the way say() escapes, as Get-ImportRuleNames already does for rule names.

Python's tempfile.gettempdir checks TMPDIR before TEMP. A shell that exports TMPDIR on Windows would put the scratch in a folder Invoke-HarnessRaw does not search. Adding $env:TMPDIR to the folders the leaf is looked for in is a one-item change.

%TEMP% on this machine holds 26 fsa-rules-* folders from earlier harness runs, the newest made at 20:54, before this attempt. They are kept scratch from runs that no RuleCases case expected to fail, or from before HF-026 was fixed, and a person may want to clear them. This build did not touch them.
